reason: Recomputed from the metric and the in-sample FN anatomy, the gain is well below +0.002 and cannot be seen through LB noise. (1) Only 424 of 6,732 FN (6.3%) are detection-side misses where the matched end is a free track end or start, which is readmit's only domain (experiments/l2_daughternet/edge_anatomy/fn_anatomy_exp39.md). The oracle ceiling for recovering ALL of them at any peak score is 424/135,729 = +0.0031 J in-sample and about +0.003 public (0.045 FN x ~0.5 detection-side x 0.145 end-anchored). The 28 one-frame bridges are already gapfill's (>=0.5 peaks). a_never is 28.3%, not 31%. (2) The x138 readmit already takes peaks >=0.965. The [0.85,0.965) band holds maybe 15-35% of those misses (a guess; the dump histogram is unmeasured), so the ceiling is +0.0005..+0.0012 at q=1, or about +0.0003..+0.0007 at a realistic link-correctness of q~0.6. Readmit is also single-pass (at most 1 frame per open end), so long missing stretches give 1 edge per side. (3) The idea's claim that failed additions are free is wrong. The readmit runs before a relink with a 7 um tight gate and prob-0 unscored pairs, and every readmit sits within 4 um of an open end, so nearly all of them get linked rather than isolated and pruned. Evidence: leaf prune removed >=479 LINKED readmitted leaves of 1,337 (CONTEXT.md l.1511-1516). The node penalty is -0.1*J per 100% nodes, i.e. about -0.0009 per +1% nodes whatever the annotation density. The idea's own readout (1.5-3x readmits, from 1.1% of nodes) implies +0.5..+2% nodes -> -0.0004..-0.0015. Net expected about -0.001..+0.0005, plus steal risk from the global relink reshuffle. (4) Transfer: the 4 dummy clips are train-embryo crops (in-sample detector), so the pre-registered readout (nodes <= +1.5%) does not bound node growth on unseen embryos. There, lower detector confidence fills the band with both real and spurious peaks, and node cost grows with it. The public readmit step itself was 0.947 -> 0.946 (browser_research_2026-09-24.md l.194). (5) Measurement: identical notebooks scored 0.946/0.942, so the single-run sd is ~0.002-0.003. The adopt rule (>= exp56 + 0.003) would fire on noise alone ~15-20% of the time and select a change worth ~0 on private.
fix_if_any: The only form that could pay is one that adds no nodes unless they complete an edge the metric can see. (a) Do not lower READMIT_MIN_SCORE globally. Instead extend the gapfill so a band peak (>=0.85) is admitted only when it bridges an open end to an open start (gap filling). That already exists at >=0.5, so check in the exp56 dummy log whether gapfill_budget_hit fires at all, and raise MAX_ADDED_FRAC only if it does (zero-cost knob when not binding). (b) Or keep a band readmit only if, after the relink, it is linked with motion distance <= 2.5 um to an anchor whose track has >= 5 frames. Drop it otherwise, so the node count rises by <0.3%. Either variant should not take an LB slot on its own; its value (<0.001) is below the noise. At most, ride it inside a finals variant that is already being submitted for another reason, and only if the dummy-run node count rises < 0.3%.
realistic_private_gain: -0.0015 .. +0.0007 (central ~0.000; node growth likely larger on unseen embryos where band peaks are more numerous)
critical_path: Technically trivial: agent-container clones exp56 with BIOHUB_READMIT_MIN_SCORE=0.85 (0.5 h, 25 Sep). kaggle-vitalii runs the private dummy test after the GPU reset (26 Sep 00:00-01:00 UTC). Vitalii submits with the user's OK on 26 Sep ~01:00 UTC, scored ~26 Sep 09:00-11:00 UTC. So it CAN be scored by the deadline, but the probe cannot resolve a <0.001 effect under ~0.003 LB noise, so the slot is wasted.
